text:
alex: ran a quick CPU flamegraph during a 2pm peak on prod-preview, saw host-side parse+tokenize at ~48% CPU overall, streaming chunking another 22%

maya: can you drop the flame link?

alex: https://perf.internal/fg/2987654321 (redacted) — key hotspot in `ingress::parse::tokenize` and grpc small-write path `grpc::Writev::emit`

ravi: nice catch. any change after the kernel-selector swap on the model nodes?

alex: we rolled kernel v3.8 yesterday morning — decode kernels look fine but host preproc got noisier. suspect batching heuristics + smaller writev chunks causing syscall pressure

lina: do we have a perf sample/snippet?

alex: pasted top lines below:
```
  48.3%  ingress_process  ingress::parse::tokenize
  22.1%  ingress_process  grpc::Writev::emit
   9.6%  ingress_process  kvcache::lookup
   6.0%  ingress_process  http::frame::serialize
```

maya: kvcache 9.6% seems ok but if tokenize is double that it's the main win. are we double-parsing anywhere?

alex: found a couple places where we tokenized in gateway + again on host when doing stream-parse fallback. short requests (<64 tokens) get pretokenized + host reparses for attachments.

ravi: can we short-circuit on a header flag from gateway that says "pretokenized: true"? avoids reparse.

lina: that flag would need sync w/ clients — but doable for internal-only traffic. non-internal still needs fallback.

maya: other lever: increase prebatch window for small requests so grpc can coalesce writev buffers. bumping from 2ms -> 5ms might reduce write syscalls. tradeoff vs latency.

alex: ran a quick sim: coalescing 2ms->5ms reduces write syscalls by ~38% and reduces writev CPU from 22% -> ~12% in sim, median p50 added +4ms for tiny requests

ravi: +4ms p50 for sub-100ms requests is ok if p95 unaffected. can we do adaptive window: only coalesce when we detect socket smallwrite surge?

lina: yes, add a short-term rate detector: if writev rate > X per second then enable coalesce for Y ms. simple token-bucket based detector.

maya: kernel selection angle: when kernel-selector picks low-latency kernels it disables some batching-friendly codepaths which amplifies syscall counts. need to ensure kernel policy keeps host preproc path with batching-friendly kernels when traffic is short-request heavy.

alex: agreed — maybe kernel policies should be workload-aware: profile sequence length distribution and prefer kernels that reduce host syscall-pressure for short seq heavy loads.

ravi: also KV cache churn: small requests often have small KV hits but lots of lookups. consider in-process LRU window per-worker to cut lookup syscall overhead for hot prefixes.

lina: be careful memory wise but implementable as a tiny TTL cache keyed by prefix-hash. 512 entries per worker should help.

maya: next steps proposed:
- add gateway header to skip host re-tokenize for internal routes (alex + ravi)
- implement adaptive writev coalesce detector (lina)
- add tiny per-worker prefix LRU cache for kv lookups (ravi)
- update kernel-selector policy to consider short-request heavy profiles (maya)

alex: i'll prototype header short-circuit today and run sandbox perf.

ravi: i'll start the LRU patch and add feature flag.

lina: coalesce detector PR coming from me, will include metrics: writev_rate, coalesce_enabled, avg_syscalls_per_request

maya: i'll sketch kernel-policy changes and a simple classifier based on recent seq-length histogram (p10/p50/p95)

sre-bot: deploy pipeline note: canary slot 7 free, suggest canary for alex gate change once PR passes tests :rocket:

alex: will open PR and add canary note. rough timeline: PR today, canary tomorrow. if numbers match sim we'll roll to prod-preview then prod.

maya: also add perf regression check: compare host flamegraphs pre/post and assert tokenize% drop > 25% for short workload.

lina: adding those asserts to perf-runner.

alex: thanks all. ping me if you want to run a local trace — I have a pprof endpoint and a small harness to replay short-request workload.

ravi: grabbing that harness now.

maya: nice triage, good roadmap. :thumbsup:
